content.text:
I submitted **index 150** (Cu 0.40, Fe 0.20, V 0.40) as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent of the three samples I measured, at 5.92 µA.

The budget allowed only three photocurrent measurements, so I tested one sample in each of three different parts of the composition range:

| Index | Cu / Fe / V | Region | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|---|
| 150 | 0.40 / 0.20 / 0.40 | Equal Cu and V, some Fe | **5.92 µA** |
| 141 | 0.53 / 0.12 / 0.35 | Cu-rich | 2.25 µA |
| 110 | 0.11 / 0.47 / 0.42 | Fe-rich (FeVO₄-like) | 1.34 µA |

How far to trust this:
- **Coverage is thin.** Three points out of 297 candidates only shows that samples with equal Cu and V beat the Cu-rich and Fe-rich ones. There could be a better composition I never measured, especially in the V-rich corner around Cu 0.1 / Fe 0.1 / V 0.8, where the library has the most samples.
- **The model checks barely shaped the choices.** Each measurement had to be preceded by a band-gap prediction from the MEGNet model. I couldn't read the full list of known phases, because it was too large to return, so I only looked up two I could guess by ID: V₂O₅ and Fe₂O₃. Both are predicted at about 2.8 eV, just above the 2.72 eV light. That suggested looking at Cu-containing compositions, but it said nothing directly about the candidates themselves.
- **XRD was not used.** All 5 XRD measurements are still unspent, so I have no phase identification for any sample.
